WAIC from paired coefficient and covariance draws

Source: R/mniw_model_comparison.R
compute_sample_waic.Rd

Evaluates row-wise multivariate normal log likelihoods for paired posterior draws, using log-sum-exp aggregation for the predictive density and sample variances for the WAIC penalty.

Usage

compute_sample_waic(Y, X, B_samples, Sigma_samples, return_log_lik = FALSE)

Arguments

Y

Finite numeric response matrix with dimensions n by q.

X

Finite numeric design matrix with dimensions n by p. Include an intercept column explicitly when required.

B_samples

Finite numeric array with dimensions p by q by S, containing posterior coefficient draws. At least two draws are required.

Sigma_samples

Finite numeric array with dimensions q by q by S, containing symmetric positive-definite posterior response covariance draws. Slice s must be paired with slice s of B_samples.

return_log_lik

Logical scalar. If TRUE, also return the S by n log_lik matrix, suitable for loo::waic() or loo::loo(). The loo package is optional and is not called by this function.

Value

The same summaries and pointwise matrix as compute_analytical_waic(), with an additional log_lik matrix when return_log_lik = TRUE.

Details

Each response row is one observation, with likelihood \(Y_i\mid B,\Sigma\sim N_q(x_i B,\Sigma)\) independently across rows. The draws can come from any posterior with this likelihood; they need not follow an MNIW law. The analytical comparison requires an MNIW posterior. Arrays retain three dimensions even when p, q, or n equals one. The penalty uses sample variance with denominator S - 1, matching loo::waic() for a matrix of log likelihoods. Correlated draws can increase Monte Carlo error; this function does not diagnose convergence.

See also

compute_analytical_waic()

Author

Sudipto Banerjee (original development implementation).

Examples

X <- matrix(1, 2, 1)
Y <- matrix(c(0.1, 0.3), 2, 1)
B <- array(c(0, 0.2, 0.4), c(1, 1, 3))
Sigma <- array(c(0.5, 1, 1.5), c(1, 1, 3))
score <- compute_sample_waic(Y, X, B, Sigma, return_log_lik = TRUE)
score$WAIC
#> [1] 3.759926
dim(score$log_lik)
#> [1] 3 2
